q: 1. The design criterion in R.C.C. walls is very similar to
explain: R.C.C. walls are designed for both axial and bending stresses, similar to slabs or long columns.

q: 2. The ratio of the allowable ultimate crushing stress of R.C.C. columns in bending to that of 150 mm cube strength is
explain: Columns are subjected to axial compression; older codes used 0.85fck for column sections.

q: 3. The maximum compressive strain permitted in R.C.C. columns at failure load is
explain: For pure axial compression, the strain is limited to 0.002.

q: 4. The maximum compressive strain permitted in uncracked R.C.C. columns under bending and compression is
explain: When bending is involved, the extreme fiber strain limit increases to 0.0035.

q: 5. The ratio of the ultimate load capacity of helically-reinforced concrete slender columns to that of tied columns is
explain: Helical reinforcement provides better lateral confinement to the concrete core compared to lateral ties, allowing for a 5% increase in load-carrying capacity according to standard codes.

q: 6. The reduction co-efficient applied to long columns designed by ultimate strength design as compared to that designed by working stress design is
explain: In ultimate strength design (USD), the reduction factor for buckling in long columns is generally more conservative/higher to account for the non-linear behavior of concrete at ultimate loads.

q: 7. According to I.S.: 456-2000, in the case of slender columns, the permissible stresses in steel and concrete are reduced by multiplying with a coefficient Cr given by
explain: The reduction factor Cr accounts for the buckling tendency of slender columns. The standard formula relates the effective length (le) to the least radius of gyration (rmin).

q: 8. The precast concrete piles are generally used for a maximum design load of about...... except for large prestressed piles
explain: Standard precast RC piles are typically designed for loads up to 80 tonnes. For higher loads, prestressed piles or cast-in-situ piles are preferred.

q: 9. On designing reinforced concrete piles as a column, it is considered as
options: fixed at one end and hinged at the other end
explain: A pile is usually considered fixed at the bottom (embedded in hard strata) and hinged at the top (connection with the pile cap) for effective length calculations.

q: 10. For reinforced piles having length up to 30 times its width, the main longitudinal reinforcement should not be less than ............ of the gross cross-sectional area of the pile.
explain: Code provisions for RC piles generally require a minimum longitudinal steel percentage of 1.25% to ensure structural integrity during driving and service.

q: 11. According to load factor method, the permissible load W on a short column reinforced with longitudinal bars and lateral stirrups, is
options: stress in concrete x area of concrete
stress in steel x area of steel
stress in concrete x area of concrete + stress in steel x area of steel
explain: The load factor (Ultimate Strength) method calculates capacity by summing the ultimate strengths contributed by both the concrete and the longitudinal steel.

q: 12. A column is regarded as long column if the ratio of its effective length and lateral dimension, exceeds
explain: A column is classified as 'long' (or slender) if the ratio of effective length to the least lateral dimension exceeds 12 (rounded to 15 in some older or specific texts).

q: 13. If the size of column is reduced above the floor, the main bars of the columns, are
options: bent inward at the floor level
stopped just below the floor level and separate lap bars provided
explain: Depending on the degree of offset, bars can be cranked (bent) or terminated with new starter bars provided to maintain continuity.

q: 14. If the diameter of longitudinal bars of a square column is 16 mm, the diameter of lateral ties should not be less than
explain: Lateral ties must be at least 1/4th the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar (16/4 = 4mm) but not less than 5mm (or 6mm in modern codes).

q: 15. A pre-cast pile generally used, is
explain: Square piles with chamfered corners are preferred because they are easy to cast and the chamfering prevents damage to the corners during driving.

q: 16. The minimum number of main steel bars provided is R.C.C.
explain: Building codes specify minimum bars for geometry: 4 for rectangular, 6 for circular (to maintain the shape), and usually one per corner for polygons.
